## list_files — Read, run with call_read
Lists folder entries and document IDs at a path within a container (does NOT return file contents — for content questions, use `search_knowledge`). Intended for inventory requests such as 'what files exist in X' or when the user named a specific filename. Large listings return a soft error directing you to `search_knowledge`; override with `confirmLarge: true` or paginate with `limit`. Each file shows when it was added and, if since changed, when it was updated. For the newest N entries of a folder, pass `sort: "newest"` and `limit: N`, then read them all with `get_documents`.

## memory_recall — Read, run with call_read
Read facts from memory, as of now or `asOf` a past date, from one `space`, several `spaces`, or (neither) every space you can see. In `query` put every other word for what you want (synonyms, abbreviations, full names) in one search instead of searching again; `subject` lists a subject's facts. Facts come one per line under their subject, led by a handle (f12) for memory_correct and memory_forget; a heading says when it shows all the subject's current facts. Answer from current facts unless asked about the past; includeHistory adds ended and corrected ones (when or why X changed). Pass a returned cursor back as `cursor` for more.

## list_files — Read, run with call_read
Lists folder entries and document IDs at a path within a container (does NOT return file contents — for content questions, use `search_knowledge`). Intended for inventory requests such as 'what files exist in X' or when the user named a specific filename. Large listings return a soft error directing you to `search_knowledge`; override with `confirmLarge: true` or paginate with `limit`. Each file shows when it was added and, if since changed, when it was updated. For the newest N entries of a folder, pass `sort: "newest"` and `limit: N`, then read them all with `get_documents`.
arguments schema: {"type":"object","properties":{"containerId":{"description":"Container ID or name","type":"string"},"path":{"description":"Folder path to list (default: root \u0027/\u0027)","type":["string","null"],"default":null},"limit":{"description":"Maximum number of entries to return. When set, large listings are truncated instead of returning a soft error. Recommended: 25.","type":["integer","null"],"default":null},"confirmLarge":{"description":"Set to true to confirm you intentionally want the full listing of a large folder. ## container_list — Read, run with call_read
Lists every searchable knowledge scope with its description and document count. Each entry is kind=managed (storage Connapse owns, browsable with `list_files`) or kind=source (an external system Connapse mirrors read-only — searchable, but it has no file listing). Memory spaces are not listed here: `memory_spaces` lists them. Use to discover what exists when the target is unknown; if the user already named one, call `search_knowledge` on it directly instead.
arguments schema: {"type":"object","properties":{}}

## container_delete — Destructive, run with call_destructive (a person must approve it first)
Delete a container. It must be emptied first, because deleting one deletes its stored files. External sources are not containers and cannot be deleted here.
arguments schema: {"type":"object","properties":{"containerId":{"description":"Container ID or name","type":"string"}},"required":["containerId"]}

## list_files — Read, run with call_read
Lists folder entries and document IDs at a path within a container (does NOT return file contents — for content questions, use `search_knowledge`). Intended for inventory requests such as 'what files exist in X' or when the user named a specific filename. Large listings return a soft error directing you to `search_knowledge`; override with `confirmLarge: true` or paginate with `limit`. Each file shows when it was added and, if since changed, when it was updated. For the newest N entries of a folder, pass `sort: "newest"` and `limit: N`, then read them all with `get_documents`.
arguments schema: {"type":"object","properties":{"containerId":{"description":"Container ID or name","type":"string"},"path":{"description":"Folder path to list (default: root \u0027/\u0027)","type":["string","null"],"default":null},"limit":{"description":"Maximum number of entries to return. When set, large listings are truncated instead of returning a soft error. Recommended: 25.","type":["integer","null"],"default":null},"confirmLarge":{"description":"Set to true to confirm you intentionally want the full listing of a large folder. Without this, listings exceeding the soft limit return an error directing you to \u0060search_knowledge\u0060.","type":["boolean","null"],"default":null},"sort":{"description":"Leave unset for folders by name, then files newest first. \u0022name\u0022: every entry by name, folders first, so \u0060limit\u0060 keeps the first names. \u0022newest\u0022: every entry most recently added first, so \u0060limit\u0060 keeps the newest.","type":["string","null"],"default":null}},"required":["containerId"]}

## container_list — Read, run with call_read
Lists every searchable knowledge scope with its description and document count. Each entry is kind=managed (storage Connapse owns, browsable with `list_files`) or kind=source (an external system Connapse mirrors read-only — searchable, but it has no file listing). Memory spaces are not listed here: `memory_spaces` lists them. Use to discover what exists when the target is unknown; if the user already named one, call `search_knowledge` on it directly instead.
arguments schema: {"type":"object","properties":{}}

GET /api/v1/agents/{id}/keys — List API keys for an agent, revoked ones included (Admin only)
Needs the admin:users scope.
